title: Gluing flat locally finitely presented algebraic spaces over an infinitesimal pushout
statement: Algebraic spaces and their morphisms are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]; their fibre products are [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The topology on an algebraic space is the quotient topology from a surjective etale scheme atlas. Flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $T\to T\prime$ be a thickening of schemes (a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism) and $T\to S$ an affine scheme morphism (inverse images of affine opens are affine). Let $P=S\amalg_TT\prime$ be the scheme pushout, meaning the universal compatible pair of maps from $S$ and $T\prime$. For a scheme $B$, let $\mathcal F(B)$ be the category of flat locally finitely presented algebraic spaces over $B$, with all $B$-morphisms as arrows. The base-change functor $$\mathcal F(P)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(S)\times_{\mathcal F(T)}\mathcal F(T\prime)$$ is an equivalence of categories. The category on the right has objects $(X,Y,\phi)$ with $X\in\mathcal F(S)$, $Y\in\mathcal F(T\prime)$, and $\phi:X\times_ST\cong Y\times_{T\prime}T$; arrows are pairs of morphisms compatible with $\phi$. In particular it induces a bijection on every Hom set and every such triple is isomorphic to the restrictions of an object of $\mathcal F(P)$. There is no properness, quasi-compactness, finite-order, or fibre-dimension hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 07W3, lemma-equivalence-categories-spaces-pushout-flat, part (3) and final equivalence; Tag 07SY, lemma-pushout-along-thickening-schemes, for scheme pushouts.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout], the specified scheme pushout $P$ has $S\to P$ a thickening and $T\simeq S\times_P T^+$. Here and below $T^+$ denotes the scheme called $T\prime$ in the statement. Base change gives the restriction functor $F$. For every scheme mapping to the target of a morphism of algebraic spaces, its pullback is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; hence these morphisms are representable by algebraic spaces. The base-change and composition assertions of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] therefore apply, with spaces regarded as stacks, and show that both restrictions of a flat locally finitely presented $P$-space are flat and locally finitely presented. Fibre-product functoriality [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] gives the specified identification over $T$ and its action on arrows. Thus $F$ takes values in exactly the category in the statement.

source.place: Tag 07W3, setup; scheme pushout Tag 07RT, lemma-pushout-along-thickening in more-morphisms.tex.

proof.text: For a triple $a=(X,Y,\phi)$ set $U=X\times_S T$, identified with $Y\times_{T^+}T$ by $\phi$. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-thickening-pushout], form $G(a)=Z=X\amalg_U Y$ with its map to $P$. The same statement gives canonical isomorphisms $X\simeq Z\times_P S$ and $Y\simeq Z\times_P T^+$ with the prescribed compatibility, hence a canonical isomorphism $\eta_a:a\simeq F(Z)$ in the unrestricted category of triples. A compatible pair of arrows between triples induces a unique map between their pushouts. Uniqueness on the two pieces proves preservation of identities and composition and naturality of $\eta$. This defines $G$ on morphisms; flatness of its output is proved next.

source.place: Tags 07VY and 07W0, pushout functor and its canonical recovery maps.

proof.text: Choose compatible surjective etale scheme covers $X_1\to X$ and $Y_1\to Y$ as in [lem-sfb-space-pushout-compatible-etale-charts]. Put $U_1=X_1\times_S T$ and $Z_1=X_1\amalg_{U_1}Y_1$. The cited statement makes $Z_1\to Z$ a surjective etale scheme atlas. By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], the composites $X_1\to S$ and $Y_1\to T^+$ are flat and locally finitely presented: their first factors are etale, hence smooth, flat and locally finitely presented, and their second factors have these properties by hypothesis. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-pushout-flat-patching] to these scheme morphisms over the original scheme span. It gives that $Z_1\to P$ is flat and locally finitely presented. By the chartwise meanings of these properties stipulated in the statement, using [def-weil-flat-morphism] and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] on this atlas, $Z\to P$ has both properties. Consequently $G$ restricts to the required categories and $\eta$ gives essential surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 07W3, proof of (1)-(5), specialized to (3), using 07W2 and scheme lemma 07RX.

proof.text: Let $W\to P$ be flat and locally finitely presented, put $D_W=G(F(W))$, and let $\epsilon_W:D_W\to W$ be induced by the two projections from its pieces. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $W_1\to W$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its composite to $P$ is flat by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. The two restrictions $(W_1)_S$ and $(W_1)_{T^+}$ are schemes, since $S,T^+,P,W_1$ are schemes, and form compatible surjective etale covers of $W_S,W_{T^+}$ by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [lem-sfb-space-pushout-compatible-etale-charts] their scheme pushout $Q$ has a representable surjective etale map $q:Q\to D_W$. By the flat-scheme assertion of [lem-sfb-scheme-pushout-flat-patching], its canonical map $Q\to W_1$ is an isomorphism. The composite $\epsilon_Wq$ is therefore etale: it equals the isomorphism $Q\to W_1$ followed by the atlas $W_1\to W$. The equality follows by restricting both maps to $(W_1)_S$ and $(W_1)_{T^+}$ and using the pushout universal property.

source.place: Tag 07W3, flat counit proof, choosing W_1 and applying the scheme counit of Tag 07RX.

proof.text: Here are the source-locality details for $\epsilon_W$, using only the scheme descent statement [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover]. For any representable etale scheme chart $C\to D_W$, put $R=C\times_{D_W}Q$. Since $q:Q\to D_W$ is representable surjective etale and $C$ is a scheme, its pullback $R$ is a scheme and $R\to C$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The map $R\to W$ is representable etale: $R\to Q$ is etale and $Q\to W$ was etale in the previous step, so use [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. For any scheme $L\to W$, the schemes $R_L=R\times_W L$ and $C_L=C\times_W L$ exist because the diagonal of $W$ is representable [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The map $R_L\to C_L$ is the pullback of $q$, hence surjective etale, and $R_L\to L$ is etale because $R\to W$ is representable etale. Apply the cited scheme descent with $(T,X,Y)=(L,C_L,R_L)$ to obtain that $C_L\to L$ is etale. Since $L$ is arbitrary, $C\to W$ is representable etale. Since $C$ is arbitrary, $\epsilon_W$ is chartwise etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. This argument imposes no quasi-compactness on the atlas.

source.place: Tag 07W3, application of Properties of Spaces Tag 03FS, lemma-etale-local; expanded using the scheme-source descent lemma rather than creating a new locality node.

proof.text: Write $a:W_S\to D_W$ for the inclusion of the first pushout piece. The recovery statement [lem-sfb-space-affine-thickening-pushout] says that $(a,\operatorname{pr}_S):W_S\to D_W\times_P S$ is an isomorphism. Since $\epsilon_W a:W_S\to W$ is the original projection, $F(\epsilon_W)_S$ composed with this isomorphism is $\operatorname{id}_{W_S}$. Hence $F(\epsilon_W)_S$ is an isomorphism. Fibre-product associativity [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $D_W\times_W W_S$ with $D_W\times_P S$: a pair $(d,(w,s))$ with $\epsilon_W(d)=w$ goes to $(d,s)$, with inverse $(d,s)\mapsto(d,(\epsilon_W(d),s))$. Under this identification the projection to $W_S$ is precisely $F(\epsilon_W)_S$, so the base change of the actual counit to $W_S$ is an isomorphism. The map $W_S\hookrightarrow W$ is a thickening, as the pullback of $S\hookrightarrow P$ [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout]. On scheme charts its ideal is the extended nil ideal of $S$: an element is a finite sum $\sum_{i=1}^r b_i a_i$ with $a_i^{n_i}=0$, whose power of degree $1+\sum_i(n_i-1)$ vanishes since every monomial contains some $a_i^{n_i}$. Thus this closed immersion still induces a homeomorphism without a uniform nilpotence bound. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-thickening-detects-iso] to the chartwise etale map $\epsilon_W$ from Step 5 and this thickening. The counit is an isomorphism; uniqueness on its two pushout pieces makes it natural in $W$.

source.place: Tag 07W3, final isomorphism argument; spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 05ZH applied to W_S inside W.

proof.text: For the inverse on Hom sets, write $W_i=W\times_P i$ for $i=S,T^+$, with projections $p_i:W_i\to W$, inclusions $a_i:W_i\to D_W$, and analogous primed notation. Given a compatible pair $u_i:W_i\to W'_i$, the pushout universal property [lem-sfb-space-affine-thickening-pushout] supplies a unique $g:D_W\to W'$ satisfying $g a_i=p'_i u_i$. Put $h=g\epsilon_W^{-1}$. Since $\epsilon_W a_i=p_i$, we have $h p_i=p'_i u_i$. Together with the fixed maps to $i$, this equality says that the base change of $h$ is $u_i$, by the fibre-product universal property. Conversely, for any $h:W\to W'$ with these restrictions, $(h\epsilon_W)a_i=h p_i=p'_i u_i$ for both pieces, so $h\epsilon_W=g$ by pushout uniqueness and $h=g\epsilon_W^{-1}$. Thus $F$ is bijective on every Hom set. This also verifies naturality of the counit: $\epsilon_{W'}G(F(h))=h\epsilon_W$ because the two composites agree on both pieces. Together with Steps 2--3 this proves the asserted equivalence for all morphisms, without any additional properness, quasi-compactness, finite-order or fibre-dimension hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 07W3, concluding equivalence; the Hom-set inverse is the pushout universal property.
